title: 3DPLAM, 3D-Printed Lightweight Affordable Manifold for Microbial Water Quality Testing
description:
An open-source, 3D-printable membrane filtration manifold for Escherichia coli quantification in drinking water. Its three parts (base, funnel and filter support) print without support structures on a consumer FDM printer. With a 100 mL syringe and a 0.45 µm membrane filter, they perform the membrane filtration test used in WHO and UNICEF household drinking water quality surveys.

The manifold was validated against a Millipore EZ-Fit stainless-steel manifold as the reference instrument. Water from 8 sample sites was filtered 3 times on each of 3 manifolds (72 filtrations, 16 comparisons between a printed manifold and the reference). The printed manifolds matched the reference WHO risk category in 12 of 16 comparisons, and in 15 of 16 when values within 5 % of a category boundary were accepted. 3DPLAM offers an open design that can be printed locally as an alternative route to the same measurement; it was validated against the EZ-Fit as a reference.

This archive contains the print-ready and editable geometry, the slicer profiles required for a gas-tight print, the protocol and assembly documentation, the tidied validation and material-test datasets with a codebook, and the scripts that regenerate every figure.
